fixtures.text: San Diego adopts the 2025 California Plumbing Code and modifies only one part of Chapter 4: Section 422.2.1 (signs on single-user toilet rooms). Section 422.1 and Table 422.1 are not amended, so the state's counts and the state pack's worked examples stand. The city's Technical Bulletin PLMB 4-1 (March 2023, still posted) applies Table 422.1 and adds plan-check practice: its own floor-area-per-person table (Table A: offices 200 sq ft, restaurants and dining rooms 30, schools 50, retail 200, warehouses 5,000), the 50/50 split, the women's-count rule, and the single-restroom exception for business and mercantile spaces of 50 or fewer, which it also allows for assembly spaces with fewer than 50 occupants.
fixtures.quote: The minimum number of plumbing fixtures shall be provided in per CPC Table 422.1, except those structures governed by the Office of Statewide Health Planning and Development (OSHPD) shall comply with CPC Table 4-2.

other_quotes.quote: The following Sections of the 2025 California Plumbing Code are modified by the City of San Diego: (a) Chapter 4, Plumbing Fixtures and Fittings, Section 422.2.1 Single User Toilet Facility Identification.

The total occupant load shall be determined in accordance with Occupant Load Factor Table A located in this Technical Bulletin. The occupant load factor for uses not specifically identified in Table A shall be based upon the uses listed in CBC, Table 1004.5 multiplied by 2.

TABLE A—OCCUPANT LOAD FOR PLUMBING FIXTURES ... Restaurants, dining rooms, drinking establishments, sidewalk cafe 30 ... Offices, open office areas 200 ... Schools for daycare, elementary and secondary 50 ... Retail or wholesale sales 200 ... Storage rooms and warehouses 5,000

The occupant load used for determining the minimum number of fixtures must be calculated assuming 50% male and 50% female, except where specifically not applicable to the project. The total number of required water closets for females shall be not less than the total number of required water closets and urinals for males.

Business and mercantile occupancies, as defined in the CBC, with a total occupant load of 50 or less including customers and employees, one toilet facility designed for use by no more than one person at a time shall be permitted for used by both sexes. This occupant load shall include both indoor and outdoor seating. This exception can be used for assembly use spaces with less than 50 occupants per the CBC.
Privacy partitions for water closets and urinals utilized by the public or employees are required and shall comply with CBC Section 1210.3.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the table is the state's, so the state pack's rows (counts by number of occupants) apply. Only the floor area per person differs (the city's Table A), which changes how many occupants a given floor area produces, not the count per occupant.

permit.exempt_list_quote: A Building Permit is not required for the following structures and activities ... (4) Non-fixed and movable fixtures; cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height. ... (8) Painting, papering, and similar finish work. ... (17) Repairs that involve only the replacement of components or existing work with similar materials for the purpose of maintenance, that do not have an aggregate valuation of over $1,000.00, and that do not affect any electrical or mechanical installations. Repairs exempt from permit requirements shall not include any addition, change, or modification in construction, exit facilities, or permanent fixtures or equipment. permit.rule_quote: No structure regulated by the Land Development Code shall be erected, constructed, enlarged, altered, repaired, improved, converted, permanently relocated or partially demolished unless a Building Permit has first been obtained from the Building Official, except as exempted in Sections 129.0202(b) and 129.0203.
permit.partitions_note: The list (San Diego Municipal Code section 129.0203(a), print dated 9-2026) names 'partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height' but not toilet partitions, and says nothing on whether floor-anchored or overhead-braced toilet compartments count. The exemptions do not apply to historical resources, some environmentally sensitive sites or unreinforced masonry buildings. The question is left open here.

restrooms_city.rule: San Diego writes the single-user rule into its own plumbing code: every single-user toilet room in a business, place of public accommodation or government agency must be signed as all-gender. The city's own list of amendments says this carries the state rule forward for easier access, so it adds nothing beyond the state pack's bullet. No city rule on shared all-gender rooms was found.
restrooms_city.quote: 422.2.1 Single-user Toilet Facilities Identification. Family or assisted use toilet facilities shall be identified with signage indicating use by either sex. All single-user toilet facilities in any business establishment, place of public accommodation, or state or local government agency shall be identified as all-gender toilet facilities by signage that complies with Section 11B-703.7.2.6 of the California Building Code and designated for use by no more than one occupant at a time or for family or assisted use. For the purposes of Section 422.2.1, "single-user toilet facility" means a toilet facility with no more than one water closet and one urinal with a locking mechanism controlled by the user.

other_quotes.quote: Section 422.2.1 is necessary since neither 2025 California Building Code Ch 12 nor the California Plumbing Code Ch 4 addresses signage for all gender toilet rooms. This amendment is being carried forward and is meant to provide more ready access to the State regulations.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to San Diego job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for San Diego offices, schools, hotels and laboratories, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** San Diego uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** San Diego requires a building permit to alter, repair or improve a building unless the work is exempt. Its exempt list covers "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height", "painting, papering, and similar finish work" and like-for-like repairs worth $1,000 or less, without naming toilet partitions, so ask the Development Services Department whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: San Diego counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer, or a restaurant with fewer than 50, may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, San Diego counts an office at one person per 200 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 30 square feet and a school at one per 50. Your architect or the Development Services Department sets the final number.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Privacy:** San Diego requires privacy partitions for toilets and urinals used by the public or by employees.
page.install_rule: Installers in San Diego need a California contractor license and a City of San Diego business tax certificate, and permits come from the Development Services Department. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In San Diego the contractor needs a California contractor license and a city business tax certificate.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter on building work in San Diego County that is $51.11 an hour plus $29.60 in benefits. The City of San Diego enforces prevailing wages on the public works projects it awards.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.75% in San Diego: 7.25% statewide plus a 0.5% county transportation tax. The city adds no tax of its own.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, resorts and beach facilities:** solid plastic (HDPE) or phenolic that handles wet floors and daily washdown.
